classes.defensive: the else of a lookup the same call has already proved -- a handle resolved or checked live above, an index validated at entry, the running task's own TCB, a slot the face wrote two lines up. The C indexes directly and has no such branch, so there is nothing to compare.
classes.interrupt-window: a re-check, or a 'did resuming the scheduler already yield', that only an interrupt landing BETWEEN two reads inside one call can change. The API differential delivers interrupts between calls; the corpus's exit-clocked ticks never landed there in 26 scenarios x 100,000 ticks.
classes.yield-window: two cores: a core asked to yield that has not yet taken it -- the C's taskTASK_SCHEDULED_TO_YIELD. Every harness takes a requested yield at the end of the step that asked for it, so a later call never finds one outstanding; on silicon it is the inter-processor interrupt's latency.
classes.integrity: the scheduler's stall diagnostics -- a ready list above the configured ceiling, no ready task, a state item that names no task. The C has no conforming behaviour there (it indexes out of range or asserts); Kairos stops and names the stall. No ready task is unit-tested; the other two need a corrupted list, which the safe API cannot build.
classes.exhaustion: the TCB arena is full. Kairos's arena is a compile-time size; the C (heap_3) fails a create only when malloc does, which no comparable run makes happen. The trace event is the C's own traceTASK_CREATE_FAILED. Unit-tested.
classes.debug-only: an argument of a debug_assert: release builds never evaluate it, and every compared run is a release build.
classes.c-undefined: the C configASSERTs, so the call is undefined there; Kairos refuses it instead. No C answer exists to compare with (D1's reasoning, for a refusal that is not spelled Err).
classes.config: an arm compiled for a configuration neither compared build uses (configUSE_PREEMPTION 0).
classes.pre-scheduler: vTaskSuspend of the running task before the scheduler starts: every compared run starts the scheduler before its first step.
classes.shadowed: the one-core own-task shortcut of the section-free spelling: the compared spelling (task_state_get) answers it first; only a direct caller of state_of reaches it, and there the answer is the same Running.
classes.between-lists: a live task on no list, which exists only inside a call, between a removal and an insert -- no caller can ask then.
classes.storage: two cores: Kairos keeps the C's termination list as two reap slots; the second fills only when two deletions of running tasks land before the idle task reaps. The API differential reaps after every step (the C's list makes reaping invisible), so one step holds at most one.
